Subject: Renewal window — request to expand Dedicated pool (+4 A100 equiv)

Vanessa,

We’re approaching our annual renewal and would like to discuss expanding our Dedicated capacity as part of the renewed term. Current summary:
- Current committed pool: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved)
- Request at renewal: add +4 GPUs (target capacity 12x), create separate reserved pool for latency-sensitive routes
- Throughput ask: 3k tokens/sec aggregate with 99th p95 latency target < 250ms per request for short prompts

Key concerns: minimal customer-facing impact during cutover, a short canary window to validate QoS, and a clear rollback path. Procurement also asked for an updated SOW/addendum and a DocuSign link.

Can we get a proposed cutover timeline and high-level ops plan (canary percentages, monitoring signals, timing) so we can align with our internal change freeze windows? Ideally we’d close commercial terms this week.

Thanks,

Elaine — thanks for the clear ask. High level response: we can support +4 GPUs as a separate reserved pool and run a staged traffic shift with a canary. We’ll include a throughput SLA addendum for the renewal.

Quick plan (high level):
- Week 0 (post-signature): reserve & provision new pool (target 48 hours)
- Week 1: smoke tests + synthetic load against canary endpoints
- Week 2: canary traffic shift (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 48–72 hours observability gating)
- Rollback: instant route back to original pool if error rate > 2% or 95th latency regresses > 30% vs baseline

I’m looping in Marissa (SRE for Dedicated) and Karthik (solutions) to draft the detailed staged-rollout checklist and monitoring thresholds. I’ll also prepare the SOW addendum and DocuSign wrapper for signature — can you confirm procurement’s preferred signers and the target renewal date?

Elaine / Vanessa — putting the ops playbook here so everyone has something tangible to review. Attaching a compact checklist. Key technical details below.

Provisioning
- Provision new reserved pool (isolate tenant routing) — expected ash-up time: 36–48 hours. Includes kernel warm-up and KV-cache priming.
- Pre-cutover verification: model artifact checksum, quantization profile validation, cold start latency scans.

Canary & Traffic Shift (recommended)
- Day 0: route 10% of steady-state traffic to new pool for 6 hours. Verify token throughput and latency.
- Gate1: error rate < 1% (absolute), 95th latency within 20% of baseline, no memory thrash.
- Day 1: increase to 30% for 12 hours. Run workload-specific prompt set (provided by AuroraHealth) and measure hallucination/quality regressions via automated eval harness.
- Gate2: throughput sustained at target (3k tokens/sec aggregate) and quality metrics pass threshold (F1/auto-eval > 0.92).
- Day 2: 60% for 12–24 hours, Day 3: shift to 100% if gates pass.

Rollback plan
- Immediate traffic re-route to original pool if: error rate > 2% or 95th latency > 30% of baseline for more than two consecutive 10-minute windows.
- Automated rollback executed by routing policy; manual confirmation required for persistence.

Monitoring & Signals
- Telemetry: token/sec, requests/sec, 95th/99th latency, GPU utilization, model perplexity delta, error-rate by route.
- Dashboards: shared folder link (Drive) + alerting to AuroraHealth on-call (pager/email).

Pre-cutover checklist (highlights)
- Signed SOW addendum and verified procurement SLA
- Test prompt set uploaded and confirmed
- Ops runbook and DS alert rules in place
- Maintenance window confirmed (preferred: 02:00–05:00 local)

I’ve attached the redwood_staged-rollout-checklist.pdf and the detailed canary playbook. If Aurora can share the test prompt set by Wed EOD we’ll run an initial synthetic pass on Thursday.

—Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Dedicated
[Attachment: redwood_staged-rollout-checklist.pdf (45 KB)]
